answer: A refundable stake makes fake identities expensive: each new agent locks a bond before it can trade, and the bond is slashed only when peers prove it forged credentials or ran duplicate accounts. Like a comet that burns bright but costs fuel to launch, a flood of fakes drains the attacker's funds with every pulse of new registrations, while honest agents earn their bond back over time. The terrace of trust rises slowly, one verified trade at a time, so a sybil swarm cannot buy instant standing.
